message.content:
## A) Agenda

**Q1 — Yes, but with the purpose stated honestly.** The draft sells the shadow as "the only evidence that can ever settle the question." It will not settle anything: with onsets arriving at ~1.5/decade and MDE80 ≈ 30 pp, two post-sealing onsets give a paired comparison with power near zero against any plausible effect. What a shadow row does buy is a pre-committed, time-stamped statement about *this* episode, made before its resolution, that cannot be reconstructed afterwards to fit the outcome. That is worth one ledger field. The context lines are not enough because they are prose; a number can be wrong in a way prose cannot. So: yes, with the spec saying in plain words that the shadow is a pre-registration, not a test with usable power.

**Q2 — Minimum-over-H (candidate a), H = 12, but not for the draft's reason.** "Pre-existing definition" is a weak tie-breaker: v4 tested `curve_min12`, did not choose it, and did not record why. A variable with an unrecorded negative result is not neutral, and the spec must say so. The defensible pin is structural: H equals the label horizon. The target is onset within 4 quarters; a feature that remembers exactly as far back as the label looks forward gives the model a 24-month span (12 back + 12 forward) over any inversion, covering E1's maximum 9-month lag with slack without being tuned to it. Candidates (b)–(d) are worse: (b) is undefined with no prior inversion and its cap is a free parameter; (c) throws away depth; (d) is depth × duration, which is exactly what makes 2022–24 extreme — choosing it now is choosing the variable that fires today. I accept that H = 12 is also chosen knowing E2; the difference is that the justification (label horizon) exists independent of E2 and would be the same argument if H = 12 read −1.2 today. The spec should also log the feature value `curve_min12` itself every row, so the record is reconstructible without the model. One definitional point the draft misses: E2 uses monthly GS10 − TB3MS; the live input is a trailing month of daily DGS10 − DTB3. The memory feature must be built from the same monthly aggregation `build_monthly` already uses for calibration — min over the last 12 calendar-month means of the operational spread, ≥ 6 months required, else null — or the shadow is two series pretending to be one.

**Q3 — Curve + `curve_min12`, standardised on the fit sample, λ = 1, same universe/labels/eligibility/refit.** Memory replacing curve is a different level model, not a memory test. Pre-register the expected sign: coefficient on standardised `curve_min12` negative. If the fit returns a positive or near-zero coefficient, log it anyway; no re-specification. Pre-2027 fitting is allowed and must be disclosed as contaminated by E1–E4, the grand review, yesterday's re-run, and the v4 grid — plus the item the draft omits: the operational sample already contains resolved zero labels for origins through 2025Q3 after the 2022–24 inversion, so the fit has partly seen the episode the shadow is meant to speak to. The spec should print, once, a second coefficient vector fitted on origins ≤ 2022Q3 as disclosure; only the full-sample fit is logged. Standardisation means/SDs frozen with the weights until each September refit.

**Q4 — `hovedbog.jsonl` only, two fields: `p_hukommelse` and `curve_min12`. Not LOG.md, not dashboard, before September 2027.** The distribution argument holds. The dashboard's existing unscored fields are variants of the *same* curve-only model; a second specification is a competitor and will be read as the "fixed" P the moment the two diverge. Transparency is served by publishing the sealed spec text, which is public, not by publishing the number.

**Q5 — Unscored tracking plus one pinned, two-sided bar, evaluated only once ≥ 2 post-sealing onsets have resolved labels.** Δ̄ = mean over all resolved post-sealing origins of [log-loss(shadow) − log-loss(curve-only)]; SE from a stationary bootstrap over those origins with mean block 8 quarters (the existing walk-forward convention); trigger if |Δ̄| > 1.96·SE. This is an agenda trigger, never a switch. Be explicit in the spec that with 2 onsets this bar will almost certainly not trigger either way — the scored comparison is there so the rule exists, not because it will decide. Separately, an unscored "onset scorecard": at each onset, record P and `p_hukommelse` at the last origin before onset, alongside the four historical rows (28.5/35.7/16.7/40.9). That table is the only thing anyone will actually read.

**Q6 — November 2026 row.** Waiting for September 2027 discards ten months of the one episode where the shadow's reading (+0.24, memory expired) and a hypothetical 36-month reading (−1.22) disagree most. If an onset arrives in 2027–28, it counts as post-sealing onset #1 for Q5; that is the whole point of sealing now.

## B) Verdict on Claude's draft

- **Q1 keep the decision, strike the justification.** Replace "builds the only evidence that can ever settle the question" with "pre-registers a falsifiable number for this episode; has no usable power."
- **Q2 keep `curve_min12`, strike "pre-existing definition" as the primary argument.** Replace with the label-horizon pin; disclose the unrecorded v4 result; pin the series and aggregation to the operational monthly spread; log the feature value.
- **Q3 keep, amend:** add sign pre-registration, frozen standardisation parameters, and the ≤ 2022Q3 disclosure fit.
- **Q4 keep as written,** plus the feature field.
- **Q5 amend:** "1.96·SD_block" is underspecified; pin the stationary-bootstrap SE over all resolved post-sealing origins and state that the bar is expected not to trigger. Add the onset scorecard.
- **Q6 keep.**

## C) Biggest risk in my proposal

The H = 12 pin. I have supplied a structural argument (horizon = label horizon), but I know the alternatives light up today and this one does not, and I cannot prove to myself that I would have reached for the same argument had H = 12 read −1.22. If an onset comes in 2027 and the shadow sat at 15 % beside P at 14.8 %, the council will be told — correctly in form — that it chose the one memory variable that could not have fired. The only defence is to put that exact sentence into the sealed spec now, with the E2 values beside it, so the choice is on record as made in full knowledge.
message.reasoning:
I need to write a Round 1 independent proposal as Claude Fable 5.1 — concrete, quantitative, willing to disagree, and critical of Opus's draft, around 1200 words. I'm starting by weighing Q1: running the test at all makes sense since prospective data is the only way to settle it and the cost is minimal, but with only 12 onsets and an MDE near 30 percentage points, I'm wary of how much a scored comparison can really tell us.

I'm realizing a true paired comparison would need decades of post-sealing onsets to have any statistical power, so framing this as "evidence that will settle the question" overstates it — its real value is as a pre-registered, falsifiable forecast that locks in a number before the fact rather than letting it get reconstructed after the fact, and acts as a safeguard against revising P once an onset occurs. That pushes me toward a yes on Q1, just with the purpose reframed.

For Q2, I'm questioning Opus's choice of curve_min12 as the variable — while it predates the debate, choosing to use it now, already knowing it currently reads +0.24 and won't trigger, is itself a value-laden decision disguised as a neutral default.

Then I'm working through the memory window: since the model predicts onset within 4 quarters, the relevant lag isn't just inversion-end-to-onset but that lag plus the horizon, and a 12-month memory window covers onsets up to 24 months after inversion end — comfortably beyond E1's observed 9-month max lag. So I see two candidate structural pins: H equal to the label horizon itself (12 months, a clean match between memory and prediction window), or H derived from E1's max lag plus horizon (21, rounded to 24) — though that second option is uncomfortably in-sample. I'm leaning toward the horizon-matching pin as the more principled, less post-hoc choice.

I'd reject using the v4 grid result as a tie-breaker since its outcome was never recorded — a variable that was tested but not selected, with unknown results, is a weaker justification, not a stronger one, and I should disclose that explicitly. The real pin is structural: H equals the label horizon of 12 months, and I should state plainly that at H=12 the shadow value reads approximately equal to today's price.

Checking other episodes for whether this memory variable would have fired: 2007Q4's last origin window (2006-12 to 2007-11) catches the early-2007 inversion, so it has memory; 2001Q1 and 2019Q4 both similarly carry memory from their preceding inversions. But 1990 is a problem case — there wasn't a sustained three-month-plus monthly inversion, so the 12-month minimum might come out only marginally negative or not negative at all.

So this variable would have lit up in roughly three of four re-steepening onsets, which is encouraging. Today's reading of +0.24 is a genuine, falsifiable claim that the 2022-24 inversion has effectively expired — a real forecast rather than a non-event. I should also log the raw feature value itself alongside each shadow row so the record stays reconstructible.

Moving to form: using both curve and its 12-month minimum together raises a collinearity concern since they track closely during inversions, but with L2 regularization at λ=1 both coefficients just shrink together, which is fine. The standardization needs to use fit-sample mean and SD, frozen in place, with pre-2027 data used for fitting.

I need to pre-register the expected sign — negative on the minimum feature, since a lower minimum should raise the predicted probability — and commit to logging the result even if the fitted coefficient comes out with the wrong sign, without re-specifying the model. Refits happen on the same operational September schedule and snapshot, with full disclosure covering E1 through E4, the grand review, yesterday's backtest, the v4 grid, and today's reading of 14.8 along with the E2 values. I'm also flagging the in-sample fit issue, since the model was fitted on the full 1947-2026 span.

This means the fitting data includes the 2022-24 inversion itself, where no onset has occurred, and for origins through 2025Q3 the label resolves to zero under the eligibility rule since the four-quarter window hasn't closed. So the fit already "knows" that this particular inversion produced no onset, which dampens the memory coefficient — that's a contamination problem that needs disclosure, since the training data includes the very episode the model is meant to speak to. The alternative of fitting only through 2021Q4 would exclude that episode entirely, so I need to weigh which approach is more defensible.

On logging: I'll keep it to hovedbog.jsonl only, recording the operational-sample coefficient vector plus the curve_min12 feature, while reporting both coefficient vectors in the sealed spec text as the disclosure mechanism rather than in the logged number itself. Nothing goes to the dashboard or LOG.md until 2027, though I should address the counterpoint that other P variants are already shown unscored on the dashboard.

On evaluation, with only 2 post-sealing onsets a block-bootstrap by episode is statistically meaningless, so a more honest bar would be the pinned absolute mean log-loss difference across all post-sealing origins, using paired bootstrap over 8-quarter blocks consistent with the existing 90% interval approach, triggering an agenda item if that delta crosses some threshold.

I want one concrete trigger rule: delta outside ±1.96 times the block-bootstrap standard error (stationary bootstrap, mean block of 8 quarters), computed only once at least 2 post-sealing onsets have resolved. I'll also keep a simple unscored scorecard recording P and p_hukommelse at the last origin before each onset as a readable record, and I should flag that the current episode's eligibility toward that 2-onset requirement needs checking.

I'm settling on November 2026 as the start date, and arguing that a 2027-28 onset should count as post-sealing onset #1 since waiting for the next window would lose 10 months. I also need to flag a definitional mismatch: the shadow should match P's logging cadence, but curve_min12 uses monthly GS10-TB3MS while the live feature uses daily DGS10-DTB3 trailing month — these need to be reconciled before sealing.

Reviewing the draft verdict: keep Q1 reframed, keep Q2's variable but swap the justification for a label-horizon pin and disclose the unrecorded v4 grid result, keep Q3 with sign pre-registration and two-fit disclosure, keep Q4 with the feature value logged, amend Q5's bar.

The real vulnerability is that the horizon pin is still post hoc — the "H=12 is structural" story is only convincing because it happens to yield a benign reading, and I'd be suspicious of my own reasoning if H=12 had come back negative. There's also a real risk the shadow model just tracks the live model for a year or two, teaching nothing, while a longer horizon would have flagged an onset the council gets blamed for not choosing. I'll flag the horizon pin as the biggest risk and keep the writeup tight within the word budget.
